# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 10
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 10

---

*[Hell-Tour continues and nears its end: those who persecuted Christians; liars; the proud; conclusion of the tour.]*

1. And another angel ran to meet us, joyful and bright, and said to us: "Come, I will show you the righteous who were persecuted and killed for righteousness' sake."

2. And he took us to a pleasant place, a place full of all delights, shining with the light of the sun.

3. And when we had entered into that place, I, Peter, saw all the righteous who had been persecuted and killed for righteousness' sake.

4. Their countenances were shining like the sun, and they were clothed in fine white linen, and their mouths were opened and they praised the Lord God their God.

5. And I saw the men, that is, those who had suffered for my name's sake. They were of a bright beauty, more beautiful than anything I had ever seen in all the world.

6. And their appearance was bright — their beauty great and their light was as the light of the sun.

7. And the angel Tartaruchus, who is set over the punishments, said to me: "Take a look also at those who were put to shame in the world and who were subjected to the power of men."

8. And I saw in the outer place an angel of fierce appearance who had the oversight of the punishments, and he was dressed like a black man, and he had a face shining like fire.

9. And he said to me: "You have seen those who are given rewards; now I will also show you the punishments."

10. And in that place I saw men and women who were set apart, who were in great torment, gnashing their teeth and weeping.

11. And I asked: "Who are these?"

12. And the angel said: "These are those who had on earth given themselves to riches and had neglected the poor and the hungry, and had not helped the widows and the orphans but had despised those who were servants of God."

13. "For this reason shall they be punished forever according to the will of God."

---
*EMET note: This chapter contains the APE's only named angel — Tartaruchus (v.7), the overseer of punishment, whose name derives from the Greek Tartarus. The brief glimpse of the righteous (vv.3–6) creates a diptych with the ongoing hell-tour.*
